tasks.name: Build contracts/hosts.json and scripts/hosts.py capability model
tasks.description:
Create plugins/autopilot/contracts/hosts.json (the declared/advertised capability surface per host) and plugins/autopilot/scripts/hosts.py (the capability-status data model and probe dispatch). hosts.py imports no sibling adapter module directly except via the dispatch table; it must not import controller/ code.

Location: plugins/autopilot/contracts/hosts.json (new file), plugins/autopilot/scripts/hosts.py (new file), tests/autopilot/test_host_argv.py (new file, Tess-owned).

Reuse: plugins/autopilot/scripts/review_stage.py's _write/_read helpers (atomic-ish write-then-read with explicit encoding) for any file this task writes under docs/dev/tmp/autopilot/probes/; plugins/autopilot/contracts/review-policy-v1.json's schema_version:1 + nested-object shape as the precedent for hosts.json's own shape.

Contract (verbatim from design doc docs/dev/project-management/designs/00014-autopilot-host-execution-v1-design.md, section `### hosts.py` and `### contracts/hosts.json`):

```python
CAPABILITY_NAMES = ("identity", "delegation", "isolation", "interception")

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CapabilityStatus:
    name: str                 # one of CAPABILITY_NAMES
    status: str               # "available" | "unavailable" | "unimplemented"
    reason: str | None        # set when status != "available":
                               # UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY / UNAVAILABLE_NO_AUTH
                               # for "unavailable"; None for "unimplemented"
                               # (the adapter has no check for this name at all)

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HostCapability:
    host_id: str                              # "claude" | "codex" | "gemini"
    statuses: dict[str, CapabilityStatus]      # keyed by CAPABILITY_NAMES

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProbeResult:
    host_id: str
    available: bool              # True iff the host binary/auth itself is
                                   # reachable at all; independent of any
                                   # single capability's status
    capability: HostCapability | None  # None when available is False
    probed_at: str                     # ISO 8601
    evidence_path: str | None          # path under docs/dev/tmp/autopilot/probes

UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY = "no_binary"
UNAVAILABLE_NO_AUTH = "no_auth"

def probe_host(host_id: str, *, project_root: Path) -> ProbeResult: ...
```

```json
{
  "schema_version": 1,
  "hosts": {
    "claude": {"capabilities": ["identity", "delegation", "isolation", "interception"]},
    "codex":  {"capabilities": ["identity", "delegation", "isolation"]},
    "gemini": {"capabilities": ["identity"]}
  }
}
```

Details:
- `probe_host` dispatches to `claude.probe()` / `codex.probe()` / `gemini.probe()` by `host_id` via a plain dict lookup (`{"claude": claude.probe, "codex": codex.probe, "gemini": gemini.probe}`), never dynamic import or plugin discovery. An unknown `host_id` raises `ValueError("unknown host_id: ...")` — this is a programming-error path, not an `UNAVAILABLE_*` reason.
- `probe_host` always returns a `CapabilityStatus` for every name in `CAPABILITY_NAMES` the adapter *could* check; an adapter with no check at all for one of them returns `"unimplemented"` for that entry rather than omitting the key.
- `CapabilityStatus.status == "unavailable"` is an environment fact (no binary, no auth); `status == "unimplemented"` is a build-time/contract defect (the adapter has no code path for that capability name).
- Write this task's own small unit tests in tests/autopilot/test_host_argv.py covering `probe_host` dispatch (known host_id, unknown host_id raises ValueError) using stub adapter modules (monkeypatched `probe` functions) since claude.py/codex.py/gemini.py do not exist yet (later tasks). Do not depend on the real adapter modules in this task's tests.
- hosts.py must import only stdlib plus, at most, a declared-at-call-time dispatch table — no module-level import of claude.py/codex.py/gemini.py is required for this task (the three adapters land in later tasks); use a lazy/local import inside `probe_host`, or accept the dispatch table as a constructor-time argument from the caller, so this task's tests do not require the adapter files to exist. Document the chosen approach in a one-line comment in hosts.py.

Acceptance criteria (PRD Phase 0, verbatim): hook_behavior_equivalence and effort_forwarding preserve source invariants while exposing the known effort mismatch as a corrected target case. (This task's contribution: the capability-status model this acceptance rests on is representable and testable; hook_behavior_equivalence and effort_forwarding are fully exercised once guards.py (task 6) and jobs.py (task 5) land — this task must not regress either by leaving CapabilityStatus/ProbeResult under-specified.)

Verify: `uv run --no-project --python 3.12 --with-requirements tools/autopilot/requirements-test.txt python -m pytest tests/autopilot/test_host_argv.py -q` passes; `python3 scripts/validate.py` still passes.

tasks.name: Build scripts/claude.py host adapter
tasks.description:
Implement the Claude host adapter exporting the shared four-function surface. Claude is the only host with a true in-session delegation primitive.

Location: plugins/autopilot/scripts/claude.py (new file).

Reuse: plugins/autopilot/scripts/hosts.py's ProbeResult/CapabilityStatus/HostCapability/CAPABILITY_NAMES/UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY/UNAVAILABLE_NO_AUTH (task 1, already landed) as the return/status shapes this adapter's probe() must produce.

Premise: plugins/autopilot/scripts/hosts.py exists and exports CAPABILITY_NAMES, CapabilityStatus, HostCapability, ProbeResult, UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY, UNAVAILABLE_NO_AUTH (task 1). Re-verify before acting; if absent, stop and report rather than redefining these types locally.

Contract (verbatim from design doc, section `### Per-host adapter module (claude.py, codex.py, gemini.py)` and `### hosts.py`):

```python
def probe(*, project_root: Path) -> ProbeResult:
    """STATIC checks only - binary-on-PATH, auth-file/env-var present,
    version string parses - never a live dispatch, never a real
    codex exec/Agent-tool round-trip. Probing a capability and
    EXECUTING it are different operations by design: probe() answers
    "would this work", can_delegate()/build_job_argv() are what a
    caller invokes to actually use a capability, and this PRD's own
    rule that its Python code never executes delegation applies to
    probe() too - a probe that actually ran a dispatch would violate
    that rule on every doctor.py/build-compatibility.py invocation,
    which is why it does not."""
def session_identity() -> dict | None:
    """Native session id + process identity for the CURRENT session, or
    None when this host exposes none (e.g. running outside that host)."""
def can_delegate() -> bool:
    """True iff this host supports a TRUE in-session subagent dispatch
    primitive: no new OS process, no provider-CLI invocation anywhere in
    the chain. Claude: True (the Agent tool), which the calling skill's
    own prompt invokes directly - a tool call inside the running session,
    not a subprocess."""
def build_job_argv(intent: "JobIntent") -> list[str] | None:
    """The argv this host's native CLI would need to RUN a job matching
    intent, for the standalone next-session instruction. Returns None
    when intent.role has no native entry point on this host (the
    caller reports that role as unsupported-on-host, it does not guess
    a substitute)."""
```

Each exports the identical four-function surface so hosts.py and jobs.py never branch on which module they hold. No adapter module ever calls subprocess.run/Popen on another provider's CLI. probe() must return a ProbeResult whose capability.statuses covers every name in CAPABILITY_NAMES (identity, delegation, isolation, interception) with one CapabilityStatus each.

Details:
- claude is the only host where HostCapability.statuses["interception"] can read "available" (client-native hook registration — Claude supports PreToolUse/PostToolUse/Stop hooks); check for this honestly rather than hardcoding True without a real signal (e.g. presence of a hooks configuration surface, or treat as always-available for Claude and document why in a comment, since Claude's hook mechanism is a first-class host feature unlike the other two).
- build_job_argv for claude: Claude has no CLI job-launch argv convention documented by this PRD; return None unless a concrete native entry point is specified — do not invent one.
- Do not write a dedicated test file in this task; plugins/autopilot/tests/autopilot/test_sessions.py (task 4) covers claude.py together with codex.py and gemini.py once all three exist.

Acceptance criteria (PRD Phase 1 task 1, verbatim): recursive_child_denied, no_nested_driver_cli and reviewer_isolation verify native host seams and request payloads in temporary roots. (This task's contribution: claude.py is one of the "native host seams" those scenarios exercise once jobs.py, task 5, lands; this task must not call subprocess anywhere.)

Verify: `python3 -c "import sys; sys.path.insert(0,'plugins/autopilot/scripts'); import claude; print(claude.probe(project_root=__import__('pathlib').Path('.')))"` runs without error; `python3 scripts/validate.py` still passes.

tasks.name: Build scripts/jobs.py job-request builder and ControllerSeam protocol
tasks.description:
Define the job-intent data model, the ControllerSeam protocol, its FakeSeam test implementation, and the cross-session job-request builder with mandatory recursion denial.

Location: plugins/autopilot/scripts/jobs.py (new file), tests/autopilot/test_jobs.py (new file, Tess-owned).

Reuse: none of the existing AP00012/00013 helpers apply directly to this file's shape; it is a genuinely new data model (confirmed by the design doc's reuse sweep, which found no existing job_intent/session_identity/can_delegate abstraction in the repo).

Premise: plugins/autopilot/scripts/claude.py, codex.py, gemini.py (tasks 2-4) all exist and export probe/session_identity/can_delegate/build_job_argv. Re-verify before acting.

Contract (verbatim from design doc, section `### jobs.py`):

```python
@dataclass(frozen=True)
class JobIntent:
    job_id: str                 # matches review-policy job_id ("alice", "bob", "carl", ...);
                                 # a job_id outside that file's current persona
                                 # set is a new reviewer/role being added to
                                 # policy, not a provider-named ad hoc value
    role: str                   # neutral role name, never a provider/model name
    inputs: dict                # artifact references + digests, not raw content
    isolation: str               # "fresh-context" | "fresh-session"
    tier: str                    # "haiku" | "sonnet" | "opus" | "fable"
    effort: str                  # characterized only; CLI forwarding is OV 00059
    policy_constraints: dict     # e.g. blindness, allowed-input identities

class ControllerSeam(Protocol):
    def submit_job(self, intent: JobIntent) -> dict: ...   # -> {"accepted": bool, "job_ref": str | None}
    def evaluate_guard(self, duty: "GuardDuty", context: dict) -> dict: ...
        # -> {"allowed": bool, "reason": str | None} - the authoritative
        # answer for a STATEFUL guard duty (custody, state integrity, live
        # job, review completeness). guards.py never re-implements this
        # logic locally; it only shapes context and relays the seam's
        # verdict into a GuardOutcome.

class FakeSeam:
    """Records submitted intents (submit_job) and answers evaluate_guard
    from caller-supplied fixture rules (a dict of {duty: (allowed, reason)}
    passed to its constructor) - it never launches anything and never
    implements real custody/state/review policy. The only seam
    implementation this PRD ships."""

def build_job_intent(*, job_id: str, role: str, inputs: dict,
                      isolation: str, tier: str, effort: str,
                      policy_constraints: dict) -> JobIntent: ...

def request_cross_session_job(intent: JobIntent, *, seam: ControllerSeam | None,
                                host: ModuleType, ancestry: list[dict]) -> dict:
    """Calls recursive_child_denied(intent, host=host, ancestry=ancestry)
       first and raises RecursionError if it returns True.
       seam is None  -> standalone mode: returns
         {"mode": "standalone",
          "instruction": {"argv", "intent": asdict(intent)}}
       where argv = host.build_job_argv(intent) (None if unsupported) and
       intent is the COMPLETE validated JobIntent carried verbatim - a
       host whose build_job_argv cannot express isolation or
       policy_constraints as CLI flags MUST still return the full intent
       dict with those fields intact; this function never silently drops
       them to produce a cleaner-looking argv.
       seam given -> controller-bound mode: returns
         {"mode": "controller", **seam.submit_job(intent)}.
    Never starts a process either way."""

def recursive_child_denied(intent: JobIntent, *, host: ModuleType,
                             ancestry: list[dict]) -> bool:
    """True when ancestry (the chain of {host_id, job_id} records this
    process inherited from its own launch - read from an environment
    variable or marker file the launching session set, never from ps
    or a live process-tree walk) already contains an entry whose
    host_id == host.HOST_ID AND job_id == intent.job_id. Called
    unconditionally as request_cross_session_job's first step, never
    an optional caller step."""
```

Details:
- request_cross_session_job never shells out - it only builds the instruction dict or forwards to seam.submit_job.
- Each adapter module referenced by `host: ModuleType` needs a `HOST_ID` module-level constant for recursive_child_denied's ancestry comparison; if claude.py/codex.py/gemini.py (tasks 2-4) do not already define `HOST_ID`, add it to each via a follow-up note in this task's own summary rather than silently assuming it exists - check first.
- Never call subprocess/Popen/os.exec* anywhere in this file.

Acceptance criteria (PRD Phase 1 task 1, verbatim): recursive_child_denied, no_nested_driver_cli and reviewer_isolation verify native host seams and request payloads in temporary roots. Also PRD Phase 0 (verbatim): hook_behavior_equivalence and effort_forwarding preserve source invariants while exposing the known effort mismatch as a corrected target case (this task's JobIntent.effort field is characterized-only, never CLI-forwarded - test that no code path in this file forwards `effort` to an argv or subprocess call).

Verify: `uv run --no-project --python 3.12 --with-requirements tools/autopilot/requirements-test.txt python -m pytest tests/autopilot/test_jobs.py -q` passes, including recursive_child_denied (ancestry match raises RecursionError before any argv/seam call) and no_nested_driver_cli (request_cross_session_job and every adapter's build_job_argv never call subprocess/os.exec* - patch to raise if called); `python3 scripts/validate.py` still passes.

attempts.devon_exploit: jobs.py's recursion-deny check, FakeSeam, and standalone-mode shape could all be satisfied with a hollowed-out implementation (first/last-only ancestry scan, module-name-based host-id guessing, always-rejecting FakeSeam, dropped argv/intent fields, shared argv object)

tasks.name: Build scripts/guards.py nine-duty guard library
tasks.description:
Define the nine guard duties, GuardOutcome, run_guard dispatch, and the nine _guard_<duty> functions split between stateful (relay onto seam.evaluate_guard) and pure/artifact-only (local checks only).

Location: plugins/autopilot/scripts/guards.py (new file), tests/autopilot/test_guards.py (new file, Tess-owned).

Reuse: this file re-implements enforce_prd_location.py's PRD-location-keeper rule locally for DOCUMENT_LOCATION (that script lives in the installed consumer plugin, a separate distribution this repo does not import) - do not attempt to import it.

Premise: plugins/autopilot/scripts/jobs.py exists and exports ControllerSeam (task 5). Re-verify before acting.

Contract (verbatim from design doc, section `### guards.py`):

```python
class GuardDuty(StrEnum):
    DOCUMENT_LOCATION = "document_location"
    CUSTODY_PUSH = "custody_push"
    DELEGATION = "delegation"
    POST_HANDOFF = "post_handoff"
    DEPARTURE = "departure"
    CONTEXT_REINJECTION = "context_reinjection"
    STATE_INTEGRITY = "state_integrity"
    REVIEW_COMPLETENESS = "review_completeness"
    LIVE_JOB = "live_job"

@dataclass(frozen=True)
class GuardOutcome:
    duty: GuardDuty
    allowed: bool
    reason: str | None       # set when allowed is False
    stateful: bool           # True -> this call hit seam; False -> pure/artifact-only

def run_guard(duty: GuardDuty, context: dict, *,
               seam: ControllerSeam | None) -> GuardOutcome: ...
```

run_guard dispatches to nine _guard_<duty> functions. Each is classified stateful (calls seam.evaluate_guard(duty, context) and relays its {allowed, reason} verbatim into GuardOutcome - CUSTODY_PUSH, STATE_INTEGRITY, LIVE_JOB, REVIEW_COMPLETENESS) or pure/artifact-only (DOCUMENT_LOCATION, DELEGATION, POST_HANDOFF, DEPARTURE, CONTEXT_REINJECTION - these check local artifacts/markers only and decide allowed themselves). A pure guard's function signature has no seam parameter at all. A stateful duty called with seam=None returns GuardOutcome(allowed=False, reason="missing_controller_seam", stateful=True) - refusal, never a silent pass.

Details:

Contract (verbatim from design doc, section `### contracts/hosts.json`):

`build-compatibility.py` reads contracts/hosts.json, then cross-checks it, per capability name, against the matching CapabilityStatus in the adapter's fresh probe() result:
- `status == "available"` -> included in the written compatibility/<host>.json.
- `status == "unavailable"` (no binary, no auth) -> excluded from the written bundle silently; this is the normal, expected shape of a bundle generated on a host that is not fully provisioned.
- `status == "unimplemented"` (the adapter has no check for a capability name contracts/hosts.json declares) -> build-compatibility.py exits non-zero (build failure, not a warning).

Details:
- For each host in contracts/hosts.json's `hosts` map, call that adapter's probe(), then for every capability name in that host's declared `capabilities` list, read the matching CapabilityStatus from the result and apply the three-way logic above.
- Write `compatibility/<host>.json` only for hosts whose probe produced at least the "available" capabilities subset; never hand-edit these files anywhere else.
- `test_compatibility.py` covers two PRD-named scenarios verbatim: the round-trip case ("generated bundle matches the contract minus any capability the live probe reported unavailable") and `no_coordinator_runtime_in_plugin` (static scan of scripts/*.py added by this PRD - hosts.py, claude.py, codex.py, gemini.py, jobs.py, guards.py, doctor.py, plus autopilot.py's new modes - for `while True`, a scheduler loop, or a bound TUI import; none of this PRD's modules may contain one).

tasks.name: [D1] plugins/autopilot/scripts/gemini.py
tasks.description:
Design: docs/dev/project-management/designs/00014-autopilot-host-execution-v1-rework-1-design.md

### Contract


Every signature below is verbatim-ready. Name each symbol exactly as written.
Import lines are given where a snippet needs a symbol its file does not already
import. The call style for the new constructor is always `hosts.unavailable(...)`
in `tools/`-level code and bare `unavailable(...)` inside an adapter that imports
it by name; each snippet below shows the style for its own file.

### 1. `plugins/autopilot/scripts/hosts.py`

Closes: R1 - "The gemini probe returns available=False together with a non-None capability, contradicting the ProbeResult contract ("None when available is False"). Claude and codex return None in the same state, so build-compatibility.py skips them while writing a gemini bundle."
Closes: R10 - "Availability is claimed without proof, and the claim contradicts the adapter's own code."

```python
CAPABILITY_NAMES = ("identity", "delegation", "isolation", "interception")

UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY = "no_binary"
UNAVAILABLE_NO_AUTH = "no_auth"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CapabilityStatus:
    name: str
    status: str
    reason: str | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HostCapability:
    host_id: str
    statuses: dict[str, CapabilityStatus]


CAPABILITY_STATUSES = ("supported", "unavailable", "unimplemented")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProbeResult:
    """`capability` is None exactly when `available` is False.

    `probe_kind` is always "static" in this package: every adapter probe is a
    binary-on-PATH plus auth-presence observation. A live invocation is AP 00017's
    certification work and OV 00059's managed launch, never this package's, so
    `certified` is always False here and no field of this record may be read as
    evidence that a host executed anything.

    `unavailable_reason` is non-None exactly when `available` is False.
    `authenticated` records auth presence for an available host (None when the
    host is unavailable, so auth was never checked).
    """

    host_id: str
    available: bool
    capability: HostCapability | None
    probed_at: str
    evidence_path: str | None
    probe_kind: str = "static"
    unavailable_reason: str | None = None
    authenticated: bool | None = None
    certified: bool = False

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Enforces EVERY invariant this record documents, so a defaulted
        construction site cannot serialise a contradictory state. A documented
        guarantee that construction can violate is not a guarantee."""
        if self.available:
            if self.capability is None or self.unavailable_reason is not None:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: available result must carry a capability and no reason")
            if not isinstance(self.authenticated, bool):
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: available result must record auth presence")
        else:
            if self.capability is not None or self.unavailable_reason is None:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: unavailable result must carry a reason and no capability")
            if self.authenticated is not None:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: unavailable result never checked auth")
        if self.probe_kind != "static":
            raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: this package performs only static probes")
        if self.certified is not False:
            raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: this package never certifies a host")


def unavailable(host_id: str, *, probed_at: str, reason: str) -> ProbeResult:
    """The single construction site for an unavailable host: `capability` is
    always None and `reason` is always recorded, so no adapter can break the
    ProbeResult invariant or drop the no_binary/no_auth distinction."""
    return ProbeResult(
        host_id=host_id,
        available=False,
        capability=None,
        probed_at=probed_at,
        evidence_path=None,
        unavailable_reason=reason,
        authenticated=None,
    )


def statuses_from(
    implemented: frozenset[str], *, authenticated: bool
) -> dict[str, CapabilityStatus]:
    """Capability statuses for an available host, derived from the adapter's
    own `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES`.

    A name the adapter does not implement is "unimplemented" with reason None
    (the status already says why). A name it does implement is "supported" when
    the host is authenticated, else "unavailable" with reason `no_auth`. The
    returned mapping always has exactly `CAPABILITY_NAMES` as its keys, in that
    order.

    "supported" is deliberately NOT "available". This package performs only
    static probes, so the strongest honest claim is "this adapter implements
    this capability and the host is authenticated" - never "this capability was
    observed working". A reader wanting the latter needs AP 00017's
    certification, and `ProbeResult.certified` is False precisely to say so.
    """
    statuses: dict[str, CapabilityStatus] = {}
    for name in CAPABILITY_NAMES:
        if name not in implemented:
            statuses[name] = CapabilityStatus(
                name=name, status="unimplemented", reason=None
            )
        elif authenticated:
            statuses[name] = CapabilityStatus(name=name, status="supported", reason=None)
        else:
            statuses[name] = CapabilityStatus(
                name=name, status="unavailable", reason=UNAVAILABLE_NO_AUTH
            )
    return statuses
```

`probe_kind`, `unavailable_reason`, `authenticated` and `certified` are new
fields **with defaults**, so no construction site needs new arguments - but
`__post_init__` rejects a contradictory one, so two existing fixtures must be
updated: the unavailable fakes at `test_host_argv.py:73-80` must pass
`unavailable_reason=hosts.UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY`, and the available fake at
`:62-70` must pass `authenticated=True`. Add one direct test beside them
asserting each invalid construction raises `ValueError` - a validator with no
test for its own rejections is the next thing to rot.

**There is no `"available"` status value anywhere after this change.**
`CAPABILITY_STATUSES` exists so the three-value domain has one written home and
`statuses_from` can be checked against it; it is read by §15(c)'s test, so it is
not an unused constant.

One thing deliberately NOT added: there is no new reason constant for
"unimplemented". The status string already carries that fact and a reason
repeating it adds nothing (current code already uses `reason=None` there -
`codex.py:51-53`, `gemini.py:37-39`).

### 2. Per-adapter `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES` (the code fact)

Closes: R10 - "`codex.probe` reports identity, delegation and isolation "available" whenever a binary and an auth file exist. But `codex.session_identity()` always returns None (codex.py:64) and `codex.can_delegate()` always returns False (codex.py:68)."
Closes: R11 - "The shipped compatibility bundles and changelog advertise capabilities from the builder's environment, not from verified behavior."

Each adapter module gains one module-level constant, immediately after its
`HOST_ID`:

```python
IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES: frozenset[str]
```

**The rule that decides its contents, stated once and applied to every adapter:
a capability name belongs in `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES` only when this module has
code that can make it true. A name whose backing function is unconditionally
inert does not belong, whatever the host could do in principle.**

| Adapter | `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES` | Why each exclusion |
|---|---|---|
| `claude.py` | `frozenset({"identity", "delegation", "isolation", "interception"})` | nothing excluded: `session_identity()` returns a record when `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` is set, `can_delegate()` returns `True`, and `interception` is the documented client-native hook registration |
| `codex.py` | `frozenset({"isolation"})` | `identity` excluded - `session_identity()` is `return None` (codex.py:64-65). `delegation` excluded - `can_delegate()` is `return False` (codex.py:68-69). `interception` excluded - already `unimplemented` today |
| `gemini.py` | `frozenset()` | all four excluded - `session_identity()` is `return None` (gemini.py:51-52), `can_delegate()` is `return False` (gemini.py:55-56), and `delegation`/`isolation`/`interception` are already `unimplemented` today |

`session_identity() -> dict | None` and `can_delegate() -> bool` keep their
current bodies and signatures in all three adapters. They were never the defect;
the claim made about them was.

### 3. `plugins/autopilot/scripts/codex.py`

The no-binary branch and the status block become:

```python
from hosts import (
    UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY,
    HostCapability,
    ProbeResult,
    statuses_from,
    unavailable,
)

HOST_ID = "codex"
IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES = frozenset({"isolation"})


def probe(*, project_root: Path) -> ProbeResult:
    probed_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    if shutil.which("codex") is None:
        return unavailable(HOST_ID, probed_at=probed_at, reason=UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY)
    return ProbeResult(
        host_id=HOST_ID,
        available=True,
        capability=HostCapability(
            host_id=HOST_ID,
            statuses=statuses_from(IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES, authenticated=_has_auth()),
        ),
        probed_at=probed_at,
        evidence_path=None,
        authenticated=_has_auth(),
    )
```

Compute `_has_auth()` once into a local and pass it to both call sites, rather
than calling it twice as the snippet reads for clarity.

`_has_auth()`, `_AUTH_ENV_VAR` and `_AUTH_FILE` are unchanged. The module's
existing static-only docstring is unchanged. `UNAVAILABLE_NO_AUTH` and
`CapabilityStatus` are no longer referenced here and come out of the import list.

A deliberate behaviour change: a codex binary present with no auth now reports
`available=True` with `isolation: unavailable (no_auth)`, as today - the host is
there, its capability is not usable. Only a missing binary is `available=False`.
This keeps the existing semantics; it is stated because the `unavailable()`
helper makes it easy to over-apply.

### 4. `plugins/autopilot/scripts/gemini.py`

Closes: R1 - "The gemini probe returns available=False together with a non-None capability ... Claude and codex return None in the same state, so build-compatibility.py skips them while writing a gemini bundle."

```python
"""Gemini host adapter - native host seam for the Gemini CLI.

STATIC checks only: binary-on-PATH and GEMINI_API_KEY presence. Never invokes
`gemini` as a subprocess and never performs a live dispatch. Implements no
capability yet: session identity and in-session delegation are both inert, so
IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES is empty and the declared contract is empty with it.
"""

from hosts import (
    UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY,
    HostCapability,
    ProbeResult,
    statuses_from,
    unavailable,
)

HOST_ID = "gemini"
IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES: frozenset[str] = frozenset()


def probe(*, project_root: Path) -> ProbeResult:
    probed_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    if shutil.which("gemini") is None:
        return unavailable(HOST_ID, probed_at=probed_at, reason=UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY)
    return ProbeResult(
        host_id=HOST_ID,
        available=True,
        capability=HostCapability(
            host_id=HOST_ID,
            statuses=statuses_from(IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES, authenticated=authenticated),
        ),
        probed_at=probed_at,
        evidence_path=None,
        authenticated=authenticated,
    )
```

with `authenticated = bool(os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY"))` computed once
before the return.

**The no-auth branch is deliberately gone.** Today a gemini binary with no
`GEMINI_API_KEY` returns `available=False` *with* a capability object - the exact
R1 contract violation. After this change a present binary is always
`available=True`. `UNAVAILABLE_NO_AUTH` and `CapabilityStatus` come out of the
import list; `os` stays.

**`GEMINI_API_KEY` presence stays observable, through the `authenticated`
field.** With `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES` empty, every capability status is
`unimplemented` whatever the auth state, so the statuses alone cannot record it -
and the PRD requires "Missing binary/auth/capability records unavailable". The
`ProbeResult.authenticated` field added in §1 is what carries it: an
authenticated and an unauthenticated gemini host now serialise differently
(`authenticated: true` against `authenticated: false`), and §15(a) asserts both.
The field records presence only; no key, token or file content is ever stored.

Gemini declaring zero capabilities **is the explicit blocker** the PRD's
Claude-free profile paragraph demands - "A missing mandatory host capability
remains an explicit blocker to this profile's certification" - and it must be
visible in the declaration and the bundle, not only in the code.

### 5. `plugins/autopilot/scripts/claude.py`

Closes: R10 - "`claude.probe` hardcodes interception "available" (claude.py:50) with no hook registration or interception test."

```python
from hosts import (
    UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY,
    HostCapability,
    ProbeResult,
    statuses_from,
    unavailable,
)

HOST_ID = "claude"
IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES = frozenset({"identity", "delegation", "isolation", "interception"})


def probe(*, project_root: Path) -> ProbeResult:
    """STATIC checks only: binary-on-PATH and auth presence. Never a live
    dispatch, never a real Agent-tool round-trip."""
    probed_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    if shutil.which("claude") is None:
        return unavailable(HOST_ID, probed_at=probed_at, reason=UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY)
    authenticated = bool(
        os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN") or os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
    )
    return ProbeResult(
        host_id=HOST_ID,
        available=True,
        capability=HostCapability(
            host_id=HOST_ID,
            statuses=statuses_from(IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES, authenticated=authenticated),
        ),
        probed_at=probed_at,
        evidence_path=None,
        authenticated=authenticated,
    )
```

**Two deliberate losses, both acceptable.** `interception` becomes auth-gated
and reports `"supported"` rather than unconditionally `"available"`: the old
hardcode plus its comment go away, because `statuses_from` has one rule and a
per-name exception would put the R10 class of defect straight back. Hook
registration genuinely does not need auth, so an unauthenticated Claude host now
under-reports `interception` by one status - the conservative direction, and the
committed bundle is unaffected because it is derived from the declaration (§7),
not from this status.

`claude.session_identity()` keeps its body. Its docstring gains one sentence:
`CLAUDE_SESSION_ID is the Claude Code session-id environment variable; absent, this host exposes no native session identity.`
`identity` stays in `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES` and is reported `"supported"` when
authenticated: the module *has* identity code, and whether a given process is
inside a Claude session is a per-run fact that belongs in probe evidence, not in
a capability claim. `"supported"` is exactly the strength of that claim - the
adapter supports identity; this probe did not watch it work.

  keeps the declaration honest if someone widens it again.


### 1. `plugins/autopilot/scripts/hosts.py`

Closes: R1 - "The gemini probe returns available=False together with a non-None capability, contradicting the ProbeResult contract ("None when available is False"). Claude and codex return None in the same state, so build-compatibility.py skips them while writing a gemini bundle."

```python
CAPABILITY_NAMES = ("identity", "delegation", "isolation", "interception")

UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY = "no_binary"
UNAVAILABLE_NO_AUTH = "no_auth"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CapabilityStatus:
    name: str
    status: str
    reason: str | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HostCapability:
    host_id: str
    statuses: dict[str, CapabilityStatus]


CAPABILITY_STATUSES = ("supported", "unavailable", "unimplemented")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProbeResult:
    """`capability` is None exactly when `available` is False.

    `probe_kind` is always "static" in this package: every adapter probe is a
    binary-on-PATH plus auth-presence observation. A live invocation is AP 00017's
    certification work and OV 00059's managed launch, never this package's, so
    `certified` is always False here and no field of this record may be read as
    evidence that a host executed anything.

    `unavailable_reason` is non-None exactly when `available` is False.
    `authenticated` records auth presence for an available host (None when the
    host is unavailable, so auth was never checked).
    """

    host_id: str
    available: bool
    capability: HostCapability | None
    probed_at: str
    evidence_path: str | None
    probe_kind: str = "static"
    unavailable_reason: str | None = None
    authenticated: bool | None = None
    certified: bool = False

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Enforces EVERY invariant this record documents, so a defaulted
        construction site cannot serialise a contradictory state. A documented
        guarantee that construction can violate is not a guarantee."""
        if self.available:
            if self.capability is None or self.unavailable_reason is not None:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: available result must carry a capability and no reason")
            if not isinstance(self.authenticated, bool):
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: available result must record auth presence")
        else:
            if self.capability is not None or self.unavailable_reason is None:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: unavailable result must carry a reason and no capability")
            if self.authenticated is not None:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: unavailable result never checked auth")
        if self.probe_kind != "static":
            raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: this package performs only static probes")
        if self.certified is not False:
            raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: this package never certifies a host")


def unavailable(host_id: str, *, probed_at: str, reason: str) -> ProbeResult:
    """The single construction site for an unavailable host: `capability` is
    always None and `reason` is always recorded, so no adapter can break the
    ProbeResult invariant or drop the no_binary/no_auth distinction."""
    return ProbeResult(
        host_id=host_id,
        available=False,
        capability=None,
        probed_at=probed_at,
        evidence_path=None,
        unavailable_reason=reason,
        authenticated=None,
    )


def statuses_from(
    implemented: frozenset[str], *, authenticated: bool
) -> dict[str, CapabilityStatus]:
    """Capability statuses for an available host, derived from the adapter's
    own `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES`.

    A name the adapter does not implement is "unimplemented" with reason None
    (the status already says why). A name it does implement is "supported" when
    the host is authenticated, else "unavailable" with reason `no_auth`. The
    returned mapping always has exactly `CAPABILITY_NAMES` as its keys, in that
    order.

    "supported" is deliberately NOT "available". This package performs only
    static probes, so the strongest honest claim is "this adapter implements
    this capability and the host is authenticated" - never "this capability was
    observed working". A reader wanting the latter needs AP 00017's
    certification, and `ProbeResult.certified` is False precisely to say so.
    """
    statuses: dict[str, CapabilityStatus] = {}
    for name in CAPABILITY_NAMES:
        if name not in implemented:
            statuses[name] = CapabilityStatus(
                name=name, status="unimplemented", reason=None
            )
        elif authenticated:
            statuses[name] = CapabilityStatus(name=name, status="supported", reason=None)
        else:
            statuses[name] = CapabilityStatus(
                name=name, status="unavailable", reason=UNAVAILABLE_NO_AUTH
            )
    return statuses
```

`probe_kind`, `unavailable_reason`, `authenticated` and `certified` are new
fields **with defaults**, so no construction site needs new arguments - but
`__post_init__` rejects a contradictory one, so two existing fixtures must be
updated: the unavailable fakes at `test_host_argv.py:73-80` must pass
`unavailable_reason=hosts.UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY`, and the available fake at
`:62-70` must pass `authenticated=True`. Add one direct test beside them
asserting each invalid construction raises `ValueError` - a validator with no
test for its own rejections is the next thing to rot.

**There is no `"available"` status value anywhere after this change.**
`CAPABILITY_STATUSES` exists so the three-value domain has one written home and
`statuses_from` can be checked against it; it is read by §15(c)'s test, so it is
not an unused constant.

One thing deliberately NOT added: there is no new reason constant for
"unimplemented". The status string already carries that fact and a reason
repeating it adds nothing (current code already uses `reason=None` there -
`codex.py:51-53`, `gemini.py:37-39`).

### 2. Per-adapter `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES` (the code fact)

Closes: R10 - "`codex.probe` reports identity, delegation and isolation "available" whenever a binary and an auth file exist. But `codex.session_identity()` always returns None (codex.py:64) and `codex.can_delegate()` always returns False (codex.py:68)."

Each adapter module gains one module-level constant, immediately after its

**The rule that decides its contents, stated once and applied to every adapter:

```python
    return ProbeResult(
```

with `authenticated = bool(os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY"))` computed once

**The no-auth branch is deliberately gone.** Today a gemini binary with no
`GEMINI_API_KEY` returns `available=False` *with* a capability object - the exact

field.** With `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES` empty, every capability status is

authenticated and an unauthenticated gemini host now serialise differently
(`authenticated: true` against `authenticated: false`), and §15(a) asserts both.

Claude-free profile paragraph demands - "A missing mandatory host capability
remains an explicit blocker to this profile's certification" - and it must be
visible in the declaration and the bundle, not only in the code.

### 7. `tools/autopilot/build-compatibility.py`

Closes: R11 - "`tools/autopilot/build-compatibility.py` derives bundle content from live auth presence, so output varies by machine."

**The committed bundle holds the declared-and-implemented set, never the live
available set.** This is the whole of R11: an artifact in git must not change
with the builder's `~/.codex/auth.json`. Replace the body of the per-host loop:

```python
import importlib

def _implemented(host_id: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    """The adapter's own IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES - a code fact, read without
    probing, so the generated bundle cannot depend on this machine."""
    return importlib.import_module(host_id).IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES


def write_bundle(compatibility_dir: Path, host_id: str, bundle: dict) -> None:
    compatibility_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = compatibility_dir / f"{host_id}.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(bundle, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


for host_id, declaration in contract["hosts"].items():
    declared = set(declaration["capabilities"])
    implemented = _implemented(host_id)
    overclaimed = sorted(declared - implemented)
    if overclaimed:
        print(
            f"host {host_id!r}: declared capability {overclaimed[0]!r} is unimplemented",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(1)
    write_bundle(
        compatibility_dir,
        host_id,
        {
            "host_id": host_id,
            "capabilities": sorted(declared),
            "probe_kind": "static",
        },
    )
```

Three consequences, all intended:

- `hosts.probe_host` is **no longer called** by this tool. Auth presence cannot
  reach a committed file, and a host with no binary installed no longer makes the
  tool skip a bundle, so a stale positive bundle can no longer survive a lost
  binary. The `probe_result.capability is None: continue` branch is deleted.
- The existing abort on a declared-but-unimplemented capability survives, with
  the same stderr wording, and is now machine-independent. It is the check that
  keeps the declaration honest if someone widens it again.
- Every bundle gains `"probe_kind": "static"` and a trailing newline. The
  trailing newline also closes the ⚪ Carl finding R42 at no extra cost.

### 10. `tools/autopilot/probe-host.py`

Closes in part: R9 - "All adapter probes are static (`shutil.which` plus an env var or auth-file existence check). Nothing invokes a host, proves identity, isolation or interception, or records unavailable hosts." (the recording and labelling half; see `## Module placement` for what stays open and why)

The record must identify itself and must state plainly that nothing was
certified. Add `import shutil` to the import block, then:

- Resolve the winning filename FIRST, inside the pinned-fd block, so the record
  can name the path it is actually written to. `O_EXCL` replaces `O_TRUNC`:
  `O_NOFOLLOW` guards symlinks only, so `O_TRUNC` would still truncate an
  external file through a pre-existing hard link.

  ```python
  parent_fd = _pinned_parent_fd(probes_dir, project_root)
  try:
      flags = os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW
      for attempt in range(1, 11):
          filename = (
              f"{args.host_id}-{timestamp}.json"
              if attempt == 1
              else f"{args.host_id}-{timestamp}-{attempt}.json"
          )
          try:
              fd = os.open(filename, flags, 0o666, dir_fd=parent_fd)
              break
          except FileExistsError:
              if attempt == 10:
                  raise
  finally:
      os.close(parent_fd)
  ```

  The retry loop lives inside the `try`, so `parent_fd` stays open across
  attempts and is still closed exactly once.

- Build the payload AFTER the filename is decided, from the name that won:

  ```python
  relative = Path("docs/dev/tmp/autopilot/probes") / filename
  record = dataclasses.asdict(result) | {
      "evidence_path": relative.as_posix(),
      "binary_path": shutil.which(args.host_id),
  }
  payload = json.dumps(record, indent=2)
  ```

  `binary_path` is **an independent second lookup**, not the adapter's own
  resolution: the adapter already called `shutil.which` inside `probe()`, and a
  `PATH` target changing between the two calls can yield `available=True` beside
  `binary_path: None`. Do not describe it as identifying the probed executable;
  it is a non-secret observation recorded alongside the result, and a mismatch
  between the two is itself useful evidence. **No auth value, token, or file
  content is ever recorded**;
  auth presence reaches the record only as the boolean `authenticated` field and
  the `status`/`unavailable_reason` values the probe already computed. The record
  also carries `probe_kind: "static"` and `certified: false` straight from the
  dataclass, so the artifact itself says no host was invoked.

Everything else stays: the tool writes only under
`docs/dev/tmp/autopilot/probes/`, pins the parent directory fd through
`_pinned_parent_fd`, and never touches live user configuration.

### 1. `plugins/autopilot/scripts/hosts.py`

Closes: R1 - "The gemini probe returns available=False together with a non-None capability, contradicting the ProbeResult contract ("None when available is False"). Claude and codex return None in the same state, so build-compatibility.py skips them while writing a gemini bundle."
Closes: R10 - "Availability is claimed without proof, and the claim contradicts the adapter's own code."

```python
CAPABILITY_NAMES = ("identity", "delegation", "isolation", "interception")

UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY = "no_binary"
UNAVAILABLE_NO_AUTH = "no_auth"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CapabilityStatus:
    name: str
    status: str
    reason: str | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HostCapability:
    host_id: str
    statuses: dict[str, CapabilityStatus]


CAPABILITY_STATUSES = ("supported", "unavailable", "unimplemented")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProbeResult:
    """`capability` is None exactly when `available` is False.

    `probe_kind` is always "static" in this package: every adapter probe is a
    binary-on-PATH plus auth-presence observation. A live invocation is AP 00017's
    certification work and OV 00059's managed launch, never this package's, so
    `certified` is always False here and no field of this record may be read as
    evidence that a host executed anything.

    `unavailable_reason` is non-None exactly when `available` is False.
    `authenticated` records auth presence for an available host (None when the
    host is unavailable, so auth was never checked).
    """

    host_id: str
    available: bool
    capability: HostCapability | None
    probed_at: str
    evidence_path: str | None
    probe_kind: str = "static"
    unavailable_reason: str | None = None
    authenticated: bool | None = None
    certified: bool = False

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Enforces EVERY invariant this record documents, so a defaulted
        construction site cannot serialise a contradictory state. A documented
        guarantee that construction can violate is not a guarantee."""
        if self.available:
            if self.capability is None or self.unavailable_reason is not None:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: available result must carry a capability and no reason")
            if not isinstance(self.authenticated, bool):
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: available result must record auth presence")
        else:
            if self.capability is not None or self.unavailable_reason is None:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: unavailable result must carry a reason and no capability")
            if self.authenticated is not None:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: unavailable result never checked auth")
        if self.probe_kind != "static":
            raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: this package performs only static probes")
        if self.certified is not False:
            raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: this package never certifies a host")


def unavailable(host_id: str, *, probed_at: str, reason: str) -> ProbeResult:
    """The single construction site for an unavailable host: `capability` is
    always None and `reason` is always recorded, so no adapter can break the
    ProbeResult invariant or drop the no_binary/no_auth distinction."""
    return ProbeResult(
        host_id=host_id,
        available=False,
        capability=None,
        probed_at=probed_at,
        evidence_path=None,
        unavailable_reason=reason,
        authenticated=None,
    )


def statuses_from(
    implemented: frozenset[str], *, authenticated: bool
) -> dict[str, CapabilityStatus]:
    """Capability statuses for an available host, derived from the adapter's
    own `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES`.

    A name the adapter does not implement is "unimplemented" with reason None
    (the status already says why). A name it does implement is "supported" when
    the host is authenticated, else "unavailable" with reason `no_auth`. The
    returned mapping always has exactly `CAPABILITY_NAMES` as its keys, in that
    order.

    "supported" is deliberately NOT "available". This package performs only
    static probes, so the strongest honest claim is "this adapter implements
    this capability and the host is authenticated" - never "this capability was
    observed working". A reader wanting the latter needs AP 00017's
    certification, and `ProbeResult.certified` is False precisely to say so.
    """
    statuses: dict[str, CapabilityStatus] = {}
    for name in CAPABILITY_NAMES:
        if name not in implemented:
            statuses[name] = CapabilityStatus(
                name=name, status="unimplemented", reason=None
            )
        elif authenticated:
            statuses[name] = CapabilityStatus(name=name, status="supported", reason=None)
        else:
            statuses[name] = CapabilityStatus(
                name=name, status="unavailable", reason=UNAVAILABLE_NO_AUTH
            )
    return statuses
```

`probe_kind`, `unavailable_reason`, `authenticated` and `certified` are new
fields **with defaults**, so no construction site needs new arguments - but
`__post_init__` rejects a contradictory one, so two existing fixtures must be
updated: the unavailable fakes at `test_host_argv.py:73-80` must pass
`unavailable_reason=hosts.UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY`, and the available fake at
`:62-70` must pass `authenticated=True`. Add one direct test beside them
asserting each invalid construction raises `ValueError` - a validator with no
test for its own rejections is the next thing to rot.

**There is no `"available"` status value anywhere after this change.**
`CAPABILITY_STATUSES` exists so the three-value domain has one written home and
`statuses_from` can be checked against it; it is read by §15(c)'s test, so it is
not an unused constant.

One thing deliberately NOT added: there is no new reason constant for
"unimplemented". The status string already carries that fact and a reason
repeating it adds nothing (current code already uses `reason=None` there -
`codex.py:51-53`, `gemini.py:37-39`).

with `authenticated = bool(os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY"))` computed once

**The no-auth branch is deliberately gone.** Today a gemini binary with no
`GEMINI_API_KEY` returns `available=False` *with* a capability object - the exact

visible in the declaration and the bundle, not only in the code.

```python
def _implemented(host_id: str) -> frozenset[str]:

    probing, so the generated bundle cannot depend on this machine."""
    return importlib.import_module(host_id).IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES


def write_bundle(compatibility_dir: Path, host_id: str, bundle: dict) -> None:

for host_id, declaration in contract["hosts"].items():

    if overclaimed:

            file=sys.stderr,

        sys.exit(1)

        host_id,
```

The record must identify itself and must state plainly that nothing was
certified. Add `import shutil` to the import block, then:

- Resolve the winning filename FIRST, inside the pinned-fd block, so the record
  can name the path it is actually written to. `O_EXCL` replaces `O_TRUNC`:
  `O_NOFOLLOW` guards symlinks only, so `O_TRUNC` would still truncate an
  external file through a pre-existing hard link.

  ```python
  parent_fd = _pinned_parent_fd(probes_dir, project_root)
  try:
      flags = os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW
      for attempt in range(1, 11):
          filename = (
              f"{args.host_id}-{timestamp}.json"
              if attempt == 1
              else f"{args.host_id}-{timestamp}-{attempt}.json"
          )
          try:
              fd = os.open(filename, flags, 0o666, dir_fd=parent_fd)
              break
          except FileExistsError:
              if attempt == 10:
                  raise
  finally:
      os.close(parent_fd)
  ```

  The retry loop lives inside the `try`, so `parent_fd` stays open across
  attempts and is still closed exactly once.

- Build the payload AFTER the filename is decided, from the name that won:

  ```python
  relative = Path("docs/dev/tmp/autopilot/probes") / filename
  record = dataclasses.asdict(result) | {
      "evidence_path": relative.as_posix(),
      "binary_path": shutil.which(args.host_id),
  }
  payload = json.dumps(record, indent=2)
  ```

  `binary_path` is **an independent second lookup**, not the adapter's own
  resolution: the adapter already called `shutil.which` inside `probe()`, and a
  `PATH` target changing between the two calls can yield `available=True` beside
  `binary_path: None`. Do not describe it as identifying the probed executable;
  it is a non-secret observation recorded alongside the result, and a mismatch
  between the two is itself useful evidence. **No auth value, token, or file
  content is ever recorded**;
  auth presence reaches the record only as the boolean `authenticated` field and
  the `status`/`unavailable_reason` values the probe already computed. The record
  also carries `probe_kind: "static"` and `certified: false` straight from the
  dataclass, so the artifact itself says no host was invoked.

Everything else stays: the tool writes only under
`docs/dev/tmp/autopilot/probes/`, pins the parent directory fd through
`_pinned_parent_fd`, and never touches live user configuration.

Closes: R1 - "The gemini probe returns available=False together with a non-None capability, contradicting the ProbeResult contract ("None when available is False"). Claude and codex return None in the same state, so build-compatibility.py skips them while writing a gemini bundle."
Closes: R10 - "Availability is claimed without proof, and the claim contradicts the adapter's own code."

```python
CAPABILITY_NAMES = ("identity", "delegation", "isolation", "interception")

UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY = "no_binary"
UNAVAILABLE_NO_AUTH = "no_auth"


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class CapabilityStatus:
    name: str
    status: str
    reason: str | None


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class HostCapability:
    host_id: str
    statuses: dict[str, CapabilityStatus]


CAPABILITY_STATUSES = ("supported", "unavailable", "unimplemented")


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProbeResult:
    """`capability` is None exactly when `available` is False.

    `probe_kind` is always "static" in this package: every adapter probe is a
    binary-on-PATH plus auth-presence observation. A live invocation is AP 00017's
    certification work and OV 00059's managed launch, never this package's, so
    `certified` is always False here and no field of this record may be read as
    evidence that a host executed anything.

    `unavailable_reason` is non-None exactly when `available` is False.
    `authenticated` records auth presence for an available host (None when the
    host is unavailable, so auth was never checked).
    """

    host_id: str
    available: bool
    capability: HostCapability | None
    probed_at: str
    evidence_path: str | None
    probe_kind: str = "static"
    unavailable_reason: str | None = None
    authenticated: bool | None = None
    certified: bool = False

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        """Enforces EVERY invariant this record documents, so a defaulted
        construction site cannot serialise a contradictory state. A documented
        guarantee that construction can violate is not a guarantee."""
        if self.available:
            if self.capability is None or self.unavailable_reason is not None:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: available result must carry a capability and no reason")
            if not isinstance(self.authenticated, bool):
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: available result must record auth presence")
        else:
            if self.capability is not None or self.unavailable_reason is None:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: unavailable result must carry a reason and no capability")
            if self.authenticated is not None:
                raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: unavailable result never checked auth")
        if self.probe_kind != "static":
            raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: this package performs only static probes")
        if self.certified is not False:
            raise ValueError(f"{self.host_id}: this package never certifies a host")


def unavailable(host_id: str, *, probed_at: str, reason: str) -> ProbeResult:
    """The single construction site for an unavailable host: `capability` is
    always None and `reason` is always recorded, so no adapter can break the
    ProbeResult invariant or drop the no_binary/no_auth distinction."""
    return ProbeResult(
        host_id=host_id,
        available=False,
        capability=None,
        probed_at=probed_at,
        evidence_path=None,
        unavailable_reason=reason,
        authenticated=None,
    )


def statuses_from(
    implemented: frozenset[str], *, authenticated: bool
) -> dict[str, CapabilityStatus]:
    """Capability statuses for an available host, derived from the adapter's
    own `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES`.

    A name the adapter does not implement is "unimplemented" with reason None
    (the status already says why). A name it does implement is "supported" when
    the host is authenticated, else "unavailable" with reason `no_auth`. The
    returned mapping always has exactly `CAPABILITY_NAMES` as its keys, in that
    order.

    "supported" is deliberately NOT "available". This package performs only
    static probes, so the strongest honest claim is "this adapter implements
    this capability and the host is authenticated" - never "this capability was
    observed working". A reader wanting the latter needs AP 00017's
    certification, and `ProbeResult.certified` is False precisely to say so.
    """
    statuses: dict[str, CapabilityStatus] = {}
    for name in CAPABILITY_NAMES:
        if name not in implemented:
            statuses[name] = CapabilityStatus(
                name=name, status="unimplemented", reason=None
            )
        elif authenticated:
            statuses[name] = CapabilityStatus(name=name, status="supported", reason=None)
        else:
            statuses[name] = CapabilityStatus(
                name=name, status="unavailable", reason=UNAVAILABLE_NO_AUTH
            )
    return statuses
```

`probe_kind`, `unavailable_reason`, `authenticated` and `certified` are new
fields **with defaults**, so no construction site needs new arguments - but
`__post_init__` rejects a contradictory one, so two existing fixtures must be
updated: the unavailable fakes at `test_host_argv.py:73-80` must pass
`unavailable_reason=hosts.UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY`, and the available fake at
`:62-70` must pass `authenticated=True`. Add one direct test beside them
asserting each invalid construction raises `ValueError` - a validator with no
test for its own rejections is the next thing to rot.

**There is no `"available"` status value anywhere after this change.**
`CAPABILITY_STATUSES` exists so the three-value domain has one written home and
`statuses_from` can be checked against it; it is read by §15(c)'s test, so it is
not an unused constant.

One thing deliberately NOT added: there is no new reason constant for
"unimplemented". The status string already carries that fact and a reason
repeating it adds nothing (current code already uses `reason=None` there -
`codex.py:51-53`, `gemini.py:37-39`).

### 2. Per-adapter `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES` (the code fact)

Closes: R10 - "`codex.probe` reports identity, delegation and isolation "available" whenever a binary and an auth file exist. But `codex.session_identity()` always returns None (codex.py:64) and `codex.can_delegate()` always returns False (codex.py:68)."
Closes: R11 - "The shipped compatibility bundles and changelog advertise capabilities from the builder's environment, not from verified behavior."

Each adapter module gains one module-level constant, immediately after its
`HOST_ID`:

```python
IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES: frozenset[str]
```

**The rule that decides its contents, stated once and applied to every adapter:
a capability name belongs in `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES` only when this module has
code that can make it true. A name whose backing function is unconditionally
inert does not belong, whatever the host could do in principle.**

| Adapter | `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES` | Why each exclusion |
|---|---|---|
| `claude.py` | `frozenset({"identity", "delegation", "isolation", "interception"})` | nothing excluded: `session_identity()` returns a record when `CLAUDE_SESSION_ID` is set, `can_delegate()` returns `True`, and `interception` is the documented client-native hook registration |
| `codex.py` | `frozenset({"isolation"})` | `identity` excluded - `session_identity()` is `return None` (codex.py:64-65). `delegation` excluded - `can_delegate()` is `return False` (codex.py:68-69). `interception` excluded - already `unimplemented` today |
| `gemini.py` | `frozenset()` | all four excluded - `session_identity()` is `return None` (gemini.py:51-52), `can_delegate()` is `return False` (gemini.py:55-56), and `delegation`/`isolation`/`interception` are already `unimplemented` today |

`session_identity() -> dict | None` and `can_delegate() -> bool` keep their
current bodies and signatures in all three adapters. They were never the defect;
the claim made about them was.

Compute `_has_auth()` once into a local and pass it to both call sites, rather

### 4. `plugins/autopilot/scripts/gemini.py`

Closes: R1 - "The gemini probe returns available=False together with a non-None capability ... Claude and codex return None in the same state, so build-compatibility.py skips them while writing a gemini bundle."

```python
"""Gemini host adapter - native host seam for the Gemini CLI.

STATIC checks only: binary-on-PATH and GEMINI_API_KEY presence. Never invokes
`gemini` as a subprocess and never performs a live dispatch. Implements no
capability yet: session identity and in-session delegation are both inert, so
IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES is empty and the declared contract is empty with it.
"""

from hosts import (
    UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY,
    HostCapability,
    ProbeResult,
    statuses_from,
    unavailable,
)

HOST_ID = "gemini"
IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES: frozenset[str] = frozenset()


def probe(*, project_root: Path) -> ProbeResult:
    probed_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    if shutil.which("gemini") is None:
        return unavailable(HOST_ID, probed_at=probed_at, reason=UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY)
    return ProbeResult(
        host_id=HOST_ID,
        available=True,
        capability=HostCapability(
            host_id=HOST_ID,
            statuses=statuses_from(IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES, authenticated=authenticated),
        ),
        probed_at=probed_at,
        evidence_path=None,
        authenticated=authenticated,
    )
```

with `authenticated = bool(os.environ.get("GEMINI_API_KEY"))` computed once
before the return.

**The no-auth branch is deliberately gone.** Today a gemini binary with no
`GEMINI_API_KEY` returns `available=False` *with* a capability object - the exact
R1 contract violation. After this change a present binary is always
`available=True`. `UNAVAILABLE_NO_AUTH` and `CapabilityStatus` come out of the
import list; `os` stays.

**`GEMINI_API_KEY` presence stays observable, through the `authenticated`
field.** With `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES` empty, every capability status is
`unimplemented` whatever the auth state, so the statuses alone cannot record it -
and the PRD requires "Missing binary/auth/capability records unavailable". The
`ProbeResult.authenticated` field added in §1 is what carries it: an
authenticated and an unauthenticated gemini host now serialise differently
(`authenticated: true` against `authenticated: false`), and §15(a) asserts both.
The field records presence only; no key, token or file content is ever stored.

Gemini declaring zero capabilities **is the explicit blocker** the PRD's
Claude-free profile paragraph demands - "A missing mandatory host capability
remains an explicit blocker to this profile's certification" - and it must be
visible in the declaration and the bundle, not only in the code.

### 5. `plugins/autopilot/scripts/claude.py`

Closes: R10 - "`claude.probe` hardcodes interception "available" (claude.py:50) with no hook registration or interception test."

```python
from hosts import (
    UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY,
    HostCapability,
    ProbeResult,
    statuses_from,
    unavailable,
)

HOST_ID = "claude"
IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES = frozenset({"identity", "delegation", "isolation", "interception"})


def probe(*, project_root: Path) -> ProbeResult:
    """STATIC checks only: binary-on-PATH and auth presence. Never a live
    dispatch, never a real Agent-tool round-trip."""
    probed_at = datetime.now(timezone.utc).isoformat()
    if shutil.which("claude") is None:
        return unavailable(HOST_ID, probed_at=probed_at, reason=UNAVAILABLE_NO_BINARY)
    authenticated = bool(
        os.environ.get("CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN") or os.environ.get("ANTHROPIC_API_KEY")
    )
    return ProbeResult(
        host_id=HOST_ID,
        available=True,
        capability=HostCapability(
            host_id=HOST_ID,
            statuses=statuses_from(IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES, authenticated=authenticated),
        ),
        probed_at=probed_at,
        evidence_path=None,
        authenticated=authenticated,
    )
```

**Two deliberate losses, both acceptable.** `interception` becomes auth-gated
and reports `"supported"` rather than unconditionally `"available"`: the old
hardcode plus its comment go away, because `statuses_from` has one rule and a
per-name exception would put the R10 class of defect straight back. Hook
registration genuinely does not need auth, so an unauthenticated Claude host now
under-reports `interception` by one status - the conservative direction, and the
committed bundle is unaffected because it is derived from the declaration (§7),
not from this status.

`claude.session_identity()` keeps its body. Its docstring gains one sentence:
`CLAUDE_SESSION_ID is the Claude Code session-id environment variable; absent, this host exposes no native session identity.`
`identity` stays in `IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES` and is reported `"supported"` when
authenticated: the module *has* identity code, and whether a given process is
inside a Claude session is a per-run fact that belongs in probe evidence, not in
a capability claim. `"supported"` is exactly the strength of that claim - the
adapter supports identity; this probe did not watch it work.

### 7. `tools/autopilot/build-compatibility.py`

Closes: R11 - "`tools/autopilot/build-compatibility.py` derives bundle content from live auth presence, so output varies by machine."

**The committed bundle holds the declared-and-implemented set, never the live
available set.** This is the whole of R11: an artifact in git must not change
with the builder's `~/.codex/auth.json`. Replace the body of the per-host loop:

```python
import importlib

def _implemented(host_id: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    """The adapter's own IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES - a code fact, read without
    probing, so the generated bundle cannot depend on this machine."""
    return importlib.import_module(host_id).IMPLEMENTED_CAPABILITIES


def write_bundle(compatibility_dir: Path, host_id: str, bundle: dict) -> None:
    compatibility_dir.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
    path = compatibility_dir / f"{host_id}.json"
    path.write_text(json.dumps(bundle, indent=2) + "\n", encoding="utf-8")


for host_id, declaration in contract["hosts"].items():
    declared = set(declaration["capabilities"])
    implemented = _implemented(host_id)
    overclaimed = sorted(declared - implemented)
    if overclaimed:
        print(
            f"host {host_id!r}: declared capability {overclaimed[0]!r} is unimplemented",
            file=sys.stderr,
        )
        sys.exit(1)
    write_bundle(
        compatibility_dir,
        host_id,
        {
            "host_id": host_id,
            "capabilities": sorted(declared),
            "probe_kind": "static",
        },
    )
```

Three consequences, all intended:

- `hosts.probe_host` is **no longer called** by this tool. Auth presence cannot
  reach a committed file, and a host with no binary installed no longer makes the
  tool skip a bundle, so a stale positive bundle can no longer survive a lost
  binary. The `probe_result.capability is None: continue` branch is deleted.
- The existing abort on a declared-but-unimplemented capability survives, with
  the same stderr wording, and is now machine-independent. It is the check that
  keeps the declaration honest if someone widens it again.
- Every bundle gains `"probe_kind": "static"` and a trailing newline. The
  trailing newline also closes the ⚪ Carl finding R42 at no extra cost.

### 10. `tools/autopilot/probe-host.py`

Closes in part: R9 - "All adapter probes are static (`shutil.which` plus an env var or auth-file existence check). Nothing invokes a host, proves identity, isolation or interception, or records unavailable hosts." (the recording and labelling half; see `## Module placement` for what stays open and why)

The record must identify itself and must state plainly that nothing was
certified. Add `import shutil` to the import block, then:

- Resolve the winning filename FIRST, inside the pinned-fd block, so the record
  can name the path it is actually written to. `O_EXCL` replaces `O_TRUNC`:
  `O_NOFOLLOW` guards symlinks only, so `O_TRUNC` would still truncate an
  external file through a pre-existing hard link.

  ```python
  parent_fd = _pinned_parent_fd(probes_dir, project_root)
  try:
      flags = os.O_WRONLY | os.O_CREAT | os.O_EXCL | os.O_NOFOLLOW
      for attempt in range(1, 11):
          filename = (
              f"{args.host_id}-{timestamp}.json"
              if attempt == 1
              else f"{args.host_id}-{timestamp}-{attempt}.json"
          )
          try:
              fd = os.open(filename, flags, 0o666, dir_fd=parent_fd)
              break
          except FileExistsError:
              if attempt == 10:
                  raise
  finally:
      os.close(parent_fd)
  ```

  The retry loop lives inside the `try`, so `parent_fd` stays open across
  attempts and is still closed exactly once.

- Build the payload AFTER the filename is decided, from the name that won:

  ```python
  relative = Path("docs/dev/tmp/autopilot/probes") / filename
  record = dataclasses.asdict(result) | {
      "evidence_path": relative.as_posix(),
      "binary_path": shutil.which(args.host_id),
  }
  payload = json.dumps(record, indent=2)
  ```

  `binary_path` is **an independent second lookup**, not the adapter's own
  resolution: the adapter already called `shutil.which` inside `probe()`, and a
  `PATH` target changing between the two calls can yield `available=True` beside
  `binary_path: None`. Do not describe it as identifying the probed executable;
  it is a non-secret observation recorded alongside the result, and a mismatch
  between the two is itself useful evidence. **No auth value, token, or file
  content is ever recorded**;
  auth presence reaches the record only as the boolean `authenticated` field and
  the `status`/`unavailable_reason` values the probe already computed. The record
  also carries `probe_kind: "static"` and `certified: false` straight from the
  dataclass, so the artifact itself says no host was invoked.

Everything else stays: the tool writes only under
`docs/dev/tmp/autopilot/probes/`, pins the parent directory fd through
`_pinned_parent_fd`, and never touches live user configuration.

### 11. `tools/autopilot/update_helper_map.py` and `tools/autopilot/source-map.json`

Closes: R7 - "Stale source-map digests. The `plugins/autopilot/scripts/autopilot.py` and `plugins/autopilot/CHANGELOG.md` rows have `destination_blob_sha256` values that no longer match the files on disk."
Closes: R8 - "test_helper_provenance_real.py::test_generator_check_accepts_the_committed_map fails with "source-map.json is not the generated helper map"."

**R7 and R8 are one defect today, and this rework would create a second one.**

*Today.* `plugins/autopilot/scripts/autopilot.py` and
`plugins/autopilot/CHANGELOG.md` are both in `update_helper_map.REFRESHED`
(`update_helper_map.py:274-278`), and `apply()` recomputes
`destination_blob_sha256` for exactly those rows. The two digests went stale when
tasks 7 and 10 edited those files without rerunning the generator; that same
staleness is why `--check` reports "not the generated helper map". **Verified
empirically at `68418c5a`**: copy the map aside, run the generator with
`--root .`, and `--check` then exits 0; the only changed values are those two
digests plus the `evidence.artifact_sha256` of the CHANGELOG row, which is derived
from the same bytes. Every AP00014 and AP00018 row is byte-identical afterwards,
because `apply()` deep-copies the document (`:488`) and upserts only
`HELPER_PATHS` (`:499-506`). Alice's claim that "the generator does not produce
them, so the committed map drifts from the tool that owns it" is refuted by that
code path: the generator never owned those rows.

*The second defect this rework would create.* All 13 paths in
`test_helper_provenance_real.AP00014_TARGETS` currently digest their real bytes,
and this rework edits nine of them. `REFRESHED` does not list them, so after the
fixes their digests go stale and §14's new row-integrity test fails - with no
permitted repair, because hand-editing a digest is forbidden. **Resolve it by
giving the generator ownership**, which is the only option that leaves one writer:

```python
AP00014_DIGESTED = (
    "plugins/autopilot/compatibility/claude.json",
    "plugins/autopilot/compatibility/codex.json",
    "plugins/autopilot/compatibility/gemini.json",
    "plugins/autopilot/contracts/hosts.json",
    "plugins/autopilot/scripts/claude.py",
    "plugins/autopilot/scripts/codex.py",
    "plugins/autopilot/scripts/doctor.py",
    "plugins/autopilot/scripts/gemini.py",
    "plugins/autopilot/scripts/guards.py",
    "plugins/autopilot/scripts/hosts.py",
    "plugins/autopilot/scripts/jobs.py",
    "tools/autopilot/build-compatibility.py",
    "tools/autopilot/probe-host.py",
)
```

In `apply()`, after the existing `REFRESHED` loop, refresh **only the digest** of
these rows - never their `evidence`, which is AP00014's own and not this
generator's to rewrite:

```python
ap00014 = set(AP00014_DIGESTED)
for row in result["assets"]:
    if row["destination_path"] in ap00014:
        row["destination_blob_sha256"] = hashlib.sha256(
            (root / row["destination_path"]).read_bytes()
        ).hexdigest()
```

The 13 paths are exactly `AP00014_TARGETS` in
`test_helper_provenance_real.py:48-62`; keep the two lists equal. The rows stay
excluded from the frozen `OTHER_ASSETS_SHA` (that exclusion is why changing their
digests is safe), and `authored_file_owners` is untouched, so the `delivery_prd`
values stay `"00014"`.

**Then, as the LAST step of the whole rework**, after every other file edit:

```
python3 tools/autopilot/update_helper_map.py --map tools/autopilot/source-map.json
```

**Never hand-edit a `destination_blob_sha256`.** Running the generator before a
later edit re-stales the map and re-breaks R7 and R8; see
`## Risks & edge cases`.

### Contract
